title: Body position and direction words
blurb: Read the HESI A2 words for lying positions, body directions, sides and limb movements, and stop reversing supine/prone, proximal/distal and abduct/adduct.
question: A note says a patient lies supine with bilateral swelling, a bruise on the lateral thigh and a cut distal to the elbow, and must abduct her arm in therapy. Where exactly is each finding, and which way does the arm move?

teach.body: Formally, position and direction words describe how the body is lying, where a point lies relative to another, which side is involved and how a limb moves. They assume the anatomical position: standing, facing forward, palms forward. In plain English: almost every word has an opposite, and the HESI A2 offers that opposite as a distractor. Learn each word with its partner and you halve the work.

teach.caption: Prone also means 'likely' (prone to infection): the sentence decides which sense.

teach.caption: Peripheral = away from the center, toward the limbs (peripheral nerves).

teach.h: Scenario: Jordan reads a therapy note
teach.body: Jordan Price, a patient-care tech applying to a radiography program, reads: 'Patient supine. Bilateral ankle edema. Abrasion on lateral left knee; laceration 2 cm distal to the right elbow. Goal: abduct right arm to shoulder height.' He translates: lying face up; both ankles swollen; a scrape on the outer side of the left knee; a cut on the forearm side of the elbow; and the arm is to move out sideways, away from the body.

teach.text: Reversals are the HESI A2's favorite trap: supine/prone, medial/lateral, proximal/distal, anterior/posterior, superior/inferior, abduct/adduct, flex/extend. Look-alikes too: peripheral vs perineal, distal vs distended, superficial vs superior, contralateral vs collateral. Say the meaning of the word before you look at the options.

teach.h: Fast method for a direction item
items: Find the prefix or root: ab-/ad-, uni-/bi-, contra-, super-/infer-.
Recall the partner word, because it will be a distractor.
For prone, ask whether the sentence is about lying or about being likely.
Pick the meaning, not the option that just fits the injury in the story.
Supine = face up; prone = face down (or likely); recumbent = lying down; lateral = side.
Anterior/ventral = front; posterior/dorsal = back; superior = above; inferior = below.
Medial = toward midline; lateral = away; proximal = nearer trunk; distal = farther.
Unilateral one side, bilateral both, contralateral opposite; peripheral = toward the outer parts.
Abduct = away from midline; adduct = toward; flex = bend; extend = straighten.

summary: You can now read lying positions, body directions, sides and limb movements from a single word. You can also catch the reversed partner (supine/prone, proximal/distal, abduct/adduct) that the HESI A2 offers as a distractor.

A.q: Infants should be placed supine in the crib for every sleep. What is the best definition of the word "supine" in this sentence?
A.why: Supine means lying on the back, face up.

whyNot.0: On the stomach is prone, the opposite.
whyNot.3: Propped upright is not lying flat at all.

A.q: Which word means "at or toward the front of the body"?
A.why: Anterior means at or toward the front.

whyNot.0: Posterior means toward the back, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Interior means inside, a look-alike word.
whyNot.2: Superior means above or toward the head.

A.q: The mole is on the inferior edge of her left shoulder blade. What is the best definition of the word "inferior" in this sentence?
A.why: Inferior means below or toward the feet: the lower edge.

B.q: An ultrasound found a unilateral kidney stone in the 40-year-old patient. What is the best definition of the word "unilateral" in this sentence?
B.why: Unilateral means affecting one side (uni- = one).

whyNot.3: The center is medial or central; lateral words are about sides.

B.q: The physical therapist asked Ms. Diaz to extend her knee fully while seated. What is the best definition of the word "extend" in this sentence?
B.why: Extend means to straighten a joint so the angle increases.

whyNot.0: Bending a joint is flex, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Rotating turns a limb around its axis.
whyNot.2: Relaxing fits an exercise loosely, but extend means straighten.

B.q: A small lump was found on the dorsal surface of Mr. Hall's hand. What is the best definition of the word "dorsal" in this sentence?
B.why: Dorsal relates to the back or upper surface: the back of the hand.

whyNot.0: The palm side is the front (ventral or palmar) surface, the opposite.
whyNot.2: The thumb side is the lateral side of the hand.
whyNot.3: The wrist end is the proximal end of the hand.

C.q: Older adults who take sleeping pills are prone to falls at night. What is the best definition of the word "prone" in this sentence?
C.why: Prone to falls means likely to have falls; the phrase 'prone to' selects the 'likely' sense, not the lying position.

whyNot.0: Face down is the position sense of prone, which does not fit 'prone to falls.'
whyNot.2: Protected against is the opposite of prone to.
whyNot.3: Unawareness fits sleeping pills loosely, but it is not the meaning of prone.

C.q: Hip exercises that adduct the legs strengthen the muscles of the inner thigh. What is the best definition of the word "adduct" in this sentence?
C.why: Adduct means to move a limb toward the midline (ad- = toward).

whyNot.0: Moving away from the midline is abduct, the opposite.

C.q: Which pair of terms have opposite meanings?
C.why: Proximal means nearer the trunk; distal means farther from it.

whyNot.0: In humans, ventral and anterior both mean toward the front.
whyNot.2: In humans, dorsal and posterior both mean toward the back.
whyNot.3: Supine is one recumbent (lying) position, so they are not opposites.

reteach.title: Direction words on a tree
reteach.question: Picture a tree with branches. How can the trunk, branches and bark teach proximal, distal, superficial and peripheral?

blocks.body: Your trunk is the tree trunk; your arms and legs are branches. A point on a branch near the trunk is proximal; a twig far out at the tip is distal. The bark is superficial; the heartwood inside is deep. The outer leaves are peripheral; the trunk is central. The top of the tree is superior and the roots are inferior.

blocks.text: Distal is about distance along a limb, not depth. A fingertip is distal; a splinter under the skin is deep or superficial, not distal.

explain.body: Supine = on the back, face up. Prone = face down. Lateral = on one side. Recumbent = lying down in any way.

whyNot.0: Supine means lying face up, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Recumbent means lying down in any position, so it does not specify face down.
whyNot.3: Lateral describes the side or lying on one side.

explain.body: Proximal = nearer the trunk; distal = farther. Medial = toward the midline; lateral = away. Superior = above; inferior = below.

test.q: Which word means "farther from the trunk or point of attachment"?
test.why: Distal means farther from the trunk or point of attachment.

whyNot.0: Proximal means nearer the trunk, the opposite.
whyNot.2: Superior means above or toward the head.

explain.body: Unilateral = one side. Bilateral = both sides. Ipsilateral = same side. Contralateral = opposite side.

test.q: Which word means "on the opposite side of the body"?
test.why: Contralateral means on the opposite side (contra- = against).

whyNot.1: Ipsilateral means on the same side.
whyNot.3: Collateral means side by side or secondary, as in a collateral vessel.

explain.body: Abduct = move away from the midline. Adduct = move toward it. Flex = bend a joint. Extend = straighten it.

test.q: Which word means "to bend a joint so the angle decreases"?
test.why: Flex means to bend a joint so the angle between the bones decreases.

whyNot.0: Extend means to straighten, the opposite.
whyNot.2: Abduct means to move a limb away from the midline.
whyNot.3: Adduct means to move a limb toward the midline.
